content.text: Commands or effects are used in scripting to alter the target that was selected with scopes and conditions .
They appear in:

items.text: command blocks (the immediate and option sections of events , or similar: effect, creation_effect, gain_effect, success, ...)
scripted effects , which can be used to group commands into re-usable macro.

content.text: (Scripting) commands are different from console commands : though some console commands have a scripting equivalent, others do not.
Available commands depend on the current scope type.

rows: Makes a character/province convert to their current religion's parent religion.

Makes a ruler abdicate to their current heir. Since 2.7 move = no can be used to ensure that the character keeps the same liege if they end up unlanded. Fires on_new_holder_inheritance for all held titles.

Makes a ruler abdicate to an any specified character. Note: To also transfer wealth, use transfer_scaled_wealth . Also does not transfer artifacts, for that consider using inherit . Fires on_new_holder_inheritance for all held titles.

Makes a ruler abdicate to the character preferred by the target character. Picks from among those in the direct line of succession, regardless of succession laws. Target character may pick themself, if in the line of succession. Fires on_new_holder_inheritance for all held titles.
Activates a disease , which can now randomly appear. Note that there's no way to deactivate a disease.
Activates a plot, making it impossible to cancel it in the intrigue screen.

Activates/deactivates a landed title. Unlike destroyed titles ( destroy_landed_title ), deactivated titles cannot be re-created by the player or AI, except through special decisions/events, using this command. Commonly used to activate landless titles such as holy orders and religion heads.
Adds the given value to the age of the scoped character. Warning: Messing with a character's age may have unintended side effects so use with caution.
Creates an alliance between characters. Also see break_alliance .
Sets a character's ambition, if valid.
Creates a new copy of the specified artifact and adds it to the treasury of the scoped character.
Betrothes two characters who are not yet married or betrothed. Warning: Buggy behavior (source?).
Adds the specified character to the scoped bloodline.
Constructs a building in a holding. Also constructs the buildings it upgrades from, based on upgrades_from .

Adds a character modifier to the scoped character. Parameter Type Description name character modifier Required. Character modifier to apply. days/months/ years/duration int Required. How long the modifier lasts. Use duration = -1 for an indefinite duration. hidden bool Optional. Hides the modifier from the character screen. Useful for automatically expiring timers used to restrict decisions. stacking bool Optional. Used to apply a modifier more than once, with stacking effects. inherit bool Optional. Used to inherit the modifier on character death until its duration wears off.
Adds a strong, non-inheritable claim to a character.
Adds the target character as a consort to the scoped character.
Adds a history entry to the scoped great work.
Adds a modifier that applies to all members of the scoped character's dynasty. Dynasty modifiers cannot be applied with a duration and cannot stack or be hidden.
Adds an evil god name to the scoped religion.
Makes scoped character be owed a favor toward another character. Also see reverse_add_favor .
Starts a friendship between characters and, if applicable, ends an existing rivalry.
Adds a god name to the scoped religion.

Adds a holding modifier to the scoped barony. Parameter Type Description name character modifier Required. Holding modifier to apply. days/months/ years/duration int Required. How long the modifier lasts. Use duration = -1 for an indefinite duration. hidden bool Optional. Hides the modifier from the character screen. Useful for automatically expiring timers used to restrict decisions. Does not hide any effects in tooltips. stacking bool Optional. Used to apply a modifier more than once, with stacking effects. Will not combine modifier icons into a single icon.

Changes the number of settlement slots in a province. [1] Note: This only works if the county contains sufficient barony titles (as defined in landed_titles). (Eg: There will be no effect if you try to add a 7th slot to a county which only has 6 defined baronies - no new empty holding slot will be added, and num_of_max_settlements will still be 6.)
Allows scoped religion to intermarry with target religion. One-way only, so apply converse intermarry separately, if desired. Also see remove_intermarry and clear_intermarry .

Adds the specified law to the scoped title. Can optionally specify to ignore cooldown and hardcoded opinion effects (i.e. on vassals, when changing succession laws), defaulting to no and yes respectively. The cooldown has no effect when adding a succession law. Also fires the law's pass_effect and effect clauses.
Shorthand way to add a law with the cooldown timer.
Starts a romance between characters but, if applicable, does not end an existing rivalry.
Changes the offmap currency for the specified offmap power of the scoped character by the specified amount.
Changes the scope's population by the specified portion.
Adds a strong, inheritable claim to a character.

Adds a province modifier . Parameter Type Description name character modifier Required. Province modifier to apply. days/months/ years/duration int Required. How long the modifier lasts. Use duration = -1 for an indefinite duration. hidden bool Optional. Hides the modifier from the province screen. Useful for automatically expiring timers used to restrict decisions. Does not hide any effects in tooltips. stacking bool Optional. Used to apply a modifier more than once, with stacking effects. Will not combine modifier icons into a single icon.
Adds an education trait matching specified attribute or level. May pick an education trait the character already has.
Starts a rivalry between characters and, if applicable, ends an existing friendship, but does not end an existing romance.

Adds a modifier to the society of the scoped character. Cannot be removed manually. Society modifiers automatically stack if more than one is applied. Parameter Type Description name character modifier Required. Society modifier to apply. days/months/ years/duration int Required. How long the modifier lasts. Use duration = -1 for an indefinite duration.
Adds a given value to the society's current progress.
Adds a character to the list of special interests, on the outliner, found on the right side of the screen, displaying the specified localisation key. Takes characters and titles.
Marries two characters, ignoring the max number of spouses their religions allow.
See above, but makes the marriage matrilineal.
Add the scoped character to the target bloodline scope.
Adds specified amount to crusade artifact pot.
Adds specified amount to crusade gold pot.
Adds specified amount to crusade artifact pot.
Adds specified amount to crusade artifact pot.
Construct a building in a special holding (hospital, fort or trade post).  Will not add the upgrades_from buildings.
Adds a trait to the character, using an ID from the traits files. Also see remove_trait .
Adds a weak, non-inheritable claim to a character.
Adds a weak, inheritable claim to a character.
Constructs target wonder in scoped province, at stage 1 complete.
Would add/complete the current stage. If a wonder is at stage 2, it'd add stage 3 completed. If it's in the process of adding a stage, it would "merely" complete that one.
Would add/complete the upgrade specified, or if used in an upgrade scope, complete currently scoped upgrade.
Increases the number of available upgrade slots.
Sets the scoped title's adjective (used in wars, for example: "2nd French Claim War for"). Can use custom localisation. Use "" to reset a title's objective.
Adjusts the percentage of a dynamic mercenary company's income that goes to its creator.

Completes a character's ambition and fires the ambition's effect -block. Useful if an ambition's success is difficult/expensive to detect by triggers, and/or a decision/event chain or anything else that can fire effects should complete the ambition.
approve_law = <law> in a title scope starts a vote on the target law for the scoped title. approve_law = <title> in a character scope votes in favor of a law for the target title.
Makes a character back another character's plot.
Banishes the scoped character to random court, or specified character's court.
Banishes all characters of the target religion to a random court.
Changes a province/character's public religion to a random heresy of their current religion.
Changes a character's secret religion to a random heresy of their current religion.
Removes an alliance between two characters. Also see add_alliance .
Breaks the betrothal between two characters. Also see add_betrothal .

Builds a new settlement in the province. Parameter Type Description type holding type Required. castle, temple, city title landed title Optional. Defaults to the first unbuilt holding as listed in common\landed_titles. holder character Optional. Defaults to the province owner.
Cancels a character's current ambition, firing the ambition's abort_effect .
Cancels a new-style Crusade still in preparation phase.
Cancels a councillor's currently assigned task.

Ends all of a character's pregnancies instantaneously. Can be called at any time during pregnancy prior to birth. If pregnancy notification is to be avoided, must be called earlier than 2 months' pregnancy.
Moves the capital of the currently scoped character to the target province/title/county. Province must be a relative scope - does not accept province IDs and saved event targets.
Changes a character's base diplomacy. Cannot go below 0 or above 100.
Changes a character's threat. Parameter Type Description value float Infamy change. localisation loc key Localisation entry for the character's threat tooltip.
Changes a character's base intrigue. Cannot go below 0 or above 100.
Changes a character's base learning. Cannot go below 0 or above 100.
Changes a character's base martial. Cannot go below 0 or above 100.

Change the composition of a dynamic mercenary title. from is optional, and simply adds/removes the specified number of a specific unit type. Also works on pre-defined mercenary compositions, and changes those compositions directly, such that mercenary companies sharing a composition all change simultaneously (vanilla has all naval mercenary companies sharing the same composition). Does not work on holy orders.
Adds the specified amount of plot power to the scoped character's plot.
Changes a random culture technology by the specified value. Can only affect technologies that can change by at least the specified amount.
Changes a random economy technology by the specified value. Can only affect technologies that can change by at least the specified amount.
Changes a random military technology by the specified value. Can only affect technologies that can change by at least the specified amount.

Changes the currency of scope character in their society. Can optionally specify parameters for the society to change the currency of and to scale the currency changed by the society influence, reducing the amount of currency consumed (or given, but is intended for the former) by 70% when the society is at 100% influence, going linearly from 0% at 0%.
Changes a character's base stewardship. Cannot go below 0 or above 100.

Changes technology in the province (referenced in common/technology.txt), by 0.1 or larger increments. Can only affect technologies that can change by at least the specified amount. Note that nomadic rulers' tech is character based, rather than their capital province.
Changes the army size of a mercenary/adventurer title by the specified percentage (0.05 = 5%). Does not affect galleys/ships. Also works on holy orders.

Changes the specified variable by the specified value, or another variable. Can specify another scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be accessed from any scope. Also see variables .

Fires an event to scoped character. See event modding . Parameter Type Description id int Required. Event ID to fire. Use of a namespace is recommended. days/months/years int Optional. Base delay before firing the event. If not specified, event occurs instantly. random int Optional. Number of days to add randomly for the event occurrence date, closed-ended ( days to days+random ). tooltip Key Optional localisation key to show as tooltip.

Adds a chronicle entry. Normally only used on player characters, since AI chronicles are discarded when making a save game. Parameter Type Description entry key Required. Localisation key containing text to display in this chronicle entry. portrait loc Optional. Which character's portrait to display. picture gfx Optional. Event picture ID. type key Optional. Only used in events fired on on_create_chronicle_if_empty .

Adds the specified opinion modifier to the scoped clan title towards the target clan title. See also clan_reverse_opinion . Parameter Type Description name opinion modifier Required. Opinion modifier to apply. who clan title Required. Towards who this opinion modifier is directed. months/years int Optional. Overrides the pre-defined opinion modifier duration. multiplier int Optional. How many stacks of the opinion modifier to apply.
Removes the specified opinion modifier from the scoped clan title towards the target clan title.
Similar to clan_opinion , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to clan_remove_opinion , but with the scopes reversed.
Removes all opinion modifiers allowing the scoped character to banish the target character. Doesn't clear ongoing reasons, that are not caused by opinion modifiers, like excommunication.
Prevents a delayed event from firing in the future for the current scope.
Removes all traits with the education = yes parameter.
Deletes a previously saved event target.
Removes all opinion modifiers allowing the scoped character to execute the target character. Doesn't clear ongoing reasons, that are not caused by opinion modifiers, like excommunication.
Clears all flags set in the current scope that begin with the specified prefix. Note: Does not work on religion, culture, society, offmap power, bloodline, wonder and wonder upgrade scopes!
Removes the focus of a character. Also see set_focus . Also fires the focus' abort_effect -clause.
Deletes a previously saved global event target.
Deletes all previously saved global event targetse.
Resets scoped religions intermarriage options to default. One-way only, so apply converse intermarry separately, if desired. Also see add_intermarry and remove_intermarry .
Deletes a persistent event target previously saved in the current scope.
Removes all opinion modifiers allowing the scoped character to imprison the target character. Doesn't clear ongoing reasons, that are not caused by opinion modifiers, like excommunication.
Stops a character from secretly practicing a religion.
Removes all opinion modifiers allowing the scoped character to revoke the target character's titles. Doesn't clear ongoing reasons, that are not caused by opinion modifiers, like excommunication.
Disbands all troops spawned with home = scoped province led by a commander created with employer = e_rebels .
Sets positive wealth of character to 0. Does nothing to negative wealth. Can be used after transfer of money via wealth command. Alternately, consider using transfer_scaled_wealth .
Removes the specified flag from the scoped artifact.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped bloodline.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped character.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped character's dynasty.
Clears the specified flag from the current scope. Works for any scope that can store flags, unlike the more specific clr_ scope _flag commands. Note: Does not work on bloodline scope!
Removes the specified script flag from the game.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped offmap power.
Clears the specified temporary flag from the scoped offmap power.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped province.
Removes any quest with that name (and from that society, if the society name is present) belonging to the scoped character. Can optionally specify a failure parameter, considered a success otherwise.
Clears the target of the specified quest belonging to the scoped character. Does not clear the quest itself.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped title.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped wonder.
Removes the specified flag from the scoped upgrade.
Saves a culture reference on a title, to be checked with the condition with the same name. Use 0 or none to clear the reference.
Converts a holding to another holding type: castle , city , temple , tribal , nomad
Sets the scoped character's public religion to his/her secret religion, or to the target character's secret religion if a scope is used.
Copies the artifact history from the target artifact to the scoped artifact.
Low-functionality variant of set_name , which should be used instead.
Gives the scoped character one of the target's personality traits that the character doesn't already have. Ignores opposite traits!
Copies title history and de jure assimilation from the target title to the scoped title.
Copies supported laws from the target title to the scoped title. Also fires those laws' pass_effect and effect clauses.

Founds a new bloodline of the specified type. Parameter Type Description type bloodline Required. Defines the type of bloodline from which to inherit the bloodlines modifier. religion religion Optional. Associates the bloodline with a religion connecting it with the religion view. society society Optional. Associates the bloodline with a society connecting it with the society view. inheritance Optional. Overrides the base type's inheritance rules. Valid entries are all_descendants , matrilineal , patrilineal , and no_inheritance . allow_bastards bool Optional. Overrides the base type's bastard rules.

Creates a random character with specified parameters. Parameter Type Description age int Age in years, if omitted defaults to a random age from 16-23 for women and 24-38 for men. name string Name of the new character. If omitted, randomly picks a suitable name from the culture's name list. has_nickname nickname Broken. Use give_nickname in new_character instead. attributes clause martial, intrigue, diplomacy, stewardship, learning (add_)trait trait health float Base health. Defaults to 5. fertility float Base fertility. Defaults to 0.5. random_traits bool Defaults to no . female bool/random/int female = no female = random female = 40 #40% chance of being female employer title If omitted, defaults to scoped character, or owner of scoped province. religion religion Religion of the new character. Defaults to scoped character/province. culture culture/random Culture of the new character. Defaults to scoped character/province. dynasty ID/none/random/culture/actually_culture actually_culture picks a random dynasty name from the culture if there's no unused static dynasty to use. dna string To give a new character a pre-determined look, for historical characters, etc. flag flag Note: Does not support dynamic flags. genetic_father character Used for portraits, congenital trait inheritance, etc. (Note: the trait inheritance is broken, and has been since Old Gods). genetic_mother character As above. race character To set a character's graphical culture separately from their actual culture. historical bool If yes, character won't ever be pruned from the database. immortal_age int Age at which a character become immortal, if relevant.

create_character = {
    random_traits = no
    name = "Hassan"
    dynasty = random
    religion = ROOT
    culture = persian
    female = no
    age = 40
    health = 6
    fertility = 0.8

    attributes = {
        martial = 6
        diplomacy = 8
        stewardship = 9
        intrigue = 12
        learning = 12
    }

    add_trait = elusive_shadow
    add_trait = patient
    add_trait = zealous
    add_trait = scholar
    add_trait = chaste
    add_trait = temperate
}
Creates a patrician family palace for the scoped character.
Starts a feud between two clans.
Creates a fort in the specified province.
Creates a hospital in the specified province.
Forms a blood oath between two clans.
Creates a random character with diplomacy education (see create_character ).
Creates a random character with intrigue education (see create_character ).
Creates a random character with learning education (see create_character ).
Creates a random character with martial education (see create_character ).
Creates a random character with stewardship education (see create_character ).
Spawns a fully reinforced retinue type in scoped character's capital province.

Creates a dynamic title with specified parameters. Landless dynamic titles require a landed home province to both hold prisoners and to act as a fallback if the title gets destroyed. This command should be run from the home province scope, otherwise the whole court will end up stuck in province 0 when the holder dies. Parameter Type Description tier tier Required. base_title title Which title's coat-of-arms to use. copy_title_laws bool See copy_title_laws . culture culture name Key Localization key for the title name. short_name bool See title flags . ruler Key Localization key for the ruler title. ruler_female Key Localization key for the female ruler title. foa Key Localization key for the form of address in letter events. holder character Required. custom_created bool landless bool Title isn't destroyed if its holder holds no baronies/counties. temporary bool Destroyed automatically when at peace. The holder and the courtiers cannot marry or accept most other diplo-actions. rebel bool Makes the title satisfy the rebel -condition. adventurer bool Adventure titles work just as temporary titles but do not get destroyed automatically when the holder is in peace. Instead, they are destroyed whenever the holder gains another title or when the holder dies. nomad bool Makes this title a clan title. mercenary bool Makes the title function as a mercenary band. army_template composition Army composition for dynamic mercenary titles. replace_captain_on_death bool Used for dynamic mercenary titles. siphons_income_to_creator float Percentage of income given to creator for dynamic mercenary titles.
Creates a trade post in the specified province (only works if the character meets requirements such as being under their trade post limit).
Changes the culture of the current scope.
Changes a character's culture technology points by the specified amount.
Removes all of the scoped character's traits with the is_illness -flag.
Breaks free the dynamic mercenary title from its creator.

Creates casualties for an army (whole unit or a specific unit type) by either a fixed amount or percentage. They won't be displayed in a combat report. [2] [3] . Using a negative number will heal units instead. percentage seems not work properly and may not work at all on event spawned armies. Allows units' current size to exceed their maximum size. type appears to be ignored. Parameter Type Description amount float Either amount or percentage is required. percentage float type unit_type Optional. Base unit types (light_infantry, heavy_infantry, pikemen, light_cavalry, knights, archers, special_troops, galleys, light_troops, or heavy_troops).
Removes morale for the army (or adds morale with negative values). Values are percentages of the army's maximum morale, with 1.0 equal to 100%.
Sets the new de jure liege of the currently scoped title. A target character assigns that character's primary title as the new de jure liege. 0 removes a title from the existing de jure structure.
Kills the currently scoped character, optionally specifying a death reason and/or killer.
Changes a character's dynastic decadence by the specified amount.
Votes against a proposed low for target title. Also see approve_law .

Destroys the scoped or specified artifact. If a bool is used, the scope must be an artifact. If an artifact name is given, the scope should be the owner of the artifact. If they own more than one, only the first one will be destroyed. Cannot be used to destroy indestructible objects; see unsafe_destroy_artifact .
Removes the scoped bloodline from the game.
Destroys the fort in the specified province.
Destroys the hospital in the specified province.
Destroy a building in a special holding (hospital, fort or trade post).

Destroys a landed title, by making it unheld. It can later be re-created by the player or AI, at the difference of deactivating it via activate_title . Note: Count-tier titles can currently not be destroyed, even if titular and not connected to a province.
Destroys a random building in the scoped holding. If a building is given as the value, then that building will never be picked for destruction, even if it is the only one left.
Destroys scoped holding. Also see build_holding .
Destroys the trade post in the specified province.
Destroys the wonder in the currently scoped province.
Removes the spicified wonder upgrade from the scoped wonder, or if used in a wonder upgrade scope, removes the scoped upgrade.
Disables or re-enables various hostile diplomatic interactions, such as imprisonment and title.  revocation. Useful in event chains around plots, factions, etc.

Fires an event to scoped character. Can only be fired through on_actions in vanilla. See event modding . Parameter Type Description id int Required. Event ID to fire.  May use a namespace . days/months/years int Optional. Base delay before firing the event. If not specified, event occurs instantly. random int Optional. Number of days to add randomly for the event occurrence date, closed-ended ( days to days+random ). tooltip Key Optional localisation key to show as tooltip.
laws/ enforce_peace/ targeted decision/ diplomatic interaction

Disallows council voting on the specified diplomatic interaction, targeted decision, enforcing realm peace or all law groups with allowed_for_councillors = yes . Also see enable_council_voting_on_issue .

disable_council_voting_on_issue = laws
disable_council_voting_on_issue = enforce_peace
disable_council_voting_on_issue = divorce_interaction
disable_council_voting_on_issue = start_sway
Enables the allow_viking_invasion characteristic of a religion. Also see enable_prepared_invasion .
Disbands all event armies or only the armies previously created with the specified earmark via spawn_unit .

Distribute amount times the specified type of Crusade pot to all/specified Crusader(s). At least one parameter is required. Parameter Type Description type gold/prestige/piety/artifact Optional. Which pots to distribute, defaults to all pots. amount float Optional. How much of the pot(s) to distribute. Defaults to 1. who title/province Optional. Recipient of distribution, defaults to all Crusaders.
Distribute conquered titles among the (beneficiaries of) the most contributing Crusaders.

Divides the specified variable by the specified value, or another variable. Can specify another scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be accessed from any scope. Also see variables .

Sets the dynasty of scoped character. May need to been chained with recalc_succession = yes , if impacting succession. Use dynasty = father_bastard to generate a cadet dynasty, dynasty = mother_bastard to create a bastard dynasty, or dynasty = none to make the character Lowborn. Special values used in character creation ( random , culture , and actually_culture ) do not work here.
Changes a character's economy technology points by the specified amount.

Applies voting rules to titles with elective succession. These are not automatically set on starting a new game, but require manual setting, unless set in title history (see on_action event 689). Uses any voting rules defined in common/succession_voting. Also see succession .
laws/ enforce_peace/ targeted decision/ diplomatic interaction

Allows council voting on the specified diplomatic interaction, targeted decision, enforcing realm peace or all law groups with allowed_for_councillors = yes . Also see disable_council_voting_on_issue .

enable_council_voting_on_issue = laws
enable_council_voting_on_issue = enforce_peace
enable_council_voting_on_issue = divorce_interaction
enable_council_voting_on_issue = start_sway
Enables dynamically prepared invasions for that religion with allow_viking_invasion flag. Also see disable_prepared_invasion .
Ends the scoped war. Possible war endings: invalid , success , whitepeace , reverse_demand

Scoped ruler razes all patrician-held trade posts from target's realm inside their own realm, gaining wealth, and prevents patricians in the target's realm from constructing new trade posts until the embargo is lifted or the embargoing ruler dies. Note that saving and loading a game tends to break various aspects of embargos.
Alternate way to add/remove the 'excommunicated' trait.

Creates or resets the specified variable in the current scope to the value of a trigger. Can specify another scope from which to take the value. Global and local variables can be exported to from any scope. Also see variables .
Reveals or hides the identity of the father of the unborn child of the scoped pregnant character.
Changes the scoped character's base fertility, which can be negative.
Similar to move_character , but it bypasses the checks and forces the character to move. Should not be used lightly.
Scoped character gains all holdings occupied in target character's subrealm. Fires on_new_holder for all titles involved.

Scoped character gains all holdings controlled by the target enemy that are de jure part of the target title. Fires on_new_holder for all titles involved, regardless of the type used, see below. Parameter Type Description title title Required. De jure title to target. enemy character Required. Whose lands to take inside the target title. same_religion bool Optional. Only vassalise rulers of the scoped character's religion, take titles from all other rulers. anti_nomad bool Optional. Don't vassalise nomadic rulers. is_crusade bool Optional. ? Vanilla comments unclear. as_if_allied_to character Optional. Allows a different character to take land in the specified character's war (2.8) is_religious bool Optional. Same as using type = holy_war . is_revolt bool Optional. Same as using type = host . type flavour key Optional. Specify title history message for all affected titles. See gain_title .

Transfers a title to a new holder, or gives a currently unheld title to a character. Current scope and target scope must include a title and character. Regardless of the structure used, the character will gain the title and opinion bonus towards the current title holder ( opinion_granted_<tier> ). Fires on_new_holder , regardless of the type used, see below. If the current and new title holders are within the same realm, also transfers de jure vassals under the current title holder, with corresponding opinion bonus ( opinion_vassal_transfer ). If the current title holder has no other titles of equal or higher tier, also transfer all de facto vassals to the new holder. If the title currently has no holder and of a higher tier than the recipient, the recipient will become independent. Can optionally specify/override title history message using type : Parameter Title history message claim "Conquered as a Claimant" created "Created" duel "Claimed in personal combat" election "Elected" faction_demand "Installed by Faction Demand" grant "Granted" holy_war "Conquered in a Holy War" host "Conquered as an Adventurer" inheritance "Inherited" invasion "Conquered in a War" revoke "Revoked" revolt "Conquered as Leader of an Uprising" usurp "Peacefully Usurped"

Similar to gain_title , but also gives a barony title if the recipient is unlanded. If the barony title is the county capital, grants the corresponding county with it. Useful if the title is higher than count tier. If the recipient is not a ruler, requires the title to be currently held.
Changes the title's gender succession law. Valid laws: Parameter Gender law agnatic Agnatic cognatic Agnatic-Cognatic true_cognatic Absolute Cognatic enatic_cognatic Enatic-Cognatic enatic Enatic

Gives the scoped character the specified council position. The position can already be taken, replacing the current character in that position, but the scoped character cannot already have a different spot on the council. Does not check the scoped character against the position's requirements, but does check if their liege can hand out the minor title.

Gives the scoped character the specified minor title. Does not check the scoped character against the minor title's requirements. Does not respect grant limits, but cannot hand out more commander titles than allowed by defines and modifiers.
Gives the scoped character the specified nickname, overwriting an already given nickname.

Similar to gain_title . Works on all title tiers, not just kingdoms. If the target character is unlanded, also gives a random demesne county of current titleholder. Gives strong pressed claims on transferred titles to current titleholder, and negative opinion modifier for title usurpation.
Similar to gain_title , but does not apply the opinion bonuses for the title grant and transferred de jure vassals.
Changes the scoped character's base health.
Holds an instant Merchant Republic election, obeying normal election rules. Use in the scope of the current leader of the republic. Bugged, destroys or disrupts the merchant republic.

Impregnates the scoped character with the target character's child (0 sets an unknown father). If scoped character and target character are of opposite sex, will always impregnate the female character of the two. Cannot impregnate men, but can impregnate a female character with another female character's child. Depending on the relationship and marriage status of the two characters, the child may be a bastard.
See impregnate , but the child's father will not be publically known, see father_of_unborn_known (condition and command).

Imprisons the scoped character by the target character, or by their liege if used with boolean yes , or released from prison with boolean no . Identical to the prisoner command, but preferred since that is also the name of a condition.

Scoped character inherits all titles of the target character (causing a game over for a player character), adding title history text according to each title's succession law. Also inherits artifacts and tributaries. Gives strong pressed claims to the target character and weak unpressed claims to their children, but no opinion malus. Fires on_new_holder_inheritance for all held titles.
Inserts all title history from the target title before the earliest entry in the scoped title's history.
Scoped character joins the oldest defensive war in which the target character is the primary defender.
Scoped character joins the oldest defensive war in which the target character is the primary defender.
Joins the faction led by the faction leader, if it exists. To start or join an existing faction, see start_faction . Also supports the optional argument ignore_requirements = yes .
Makes the scoped character join the specified society.
(Dis)allows title holder to use matrilineal marriage. Not to be confused with set_allows_matrilineal_marriage , which adjusts a religion instead.
Makes the scoped character leave the specified faction, or all factions.
Makes the scoped character leave the target character's plot.
Makes the scoped character leave their current society.
Scoped ruler stops embargoing the target character, allowing patricians in the target's realm to once more construct trade posts in the scoped ruler's realm.

Logs information about the gamestate for debug purposes into game.log . Localisation commands can be used normally in the string. Can even be used within trigger contexts that otherwise only accept conditions , such as trigger , limit , potential and allow . Only logs if the game is started with the -debugscripts parameter.
Logs a list of the scope IDs corresponding to ROOT , all FROM s and all saved event targets, into game.log . Only logs if the game is started with the -debugscripts parameter.
Fires an event to scoped character. Uses the letter window. See character_event .
Fires an event to scoped character. Uses a bigger window. See character_event .
Toggles changing the new-style Crusade target, via interface and script.
Makes the holding the capital of the province, unless not owned by the province owner, in which case it becomes the second holding in the province. Also see revoke_capital_holding .
Makes the scoped character the primary spouse of their spouse.
Makes the scoped title the primary title of its holder.
Makes the religion's reformer the secular/temporal head of religion. Requires a corresponding landed title to be defined.

Makes the target character a tributary of the scoped character. See tributary modding . Parameter Type Description who character Required. Character who becomes the tributary. tributary_type tributary type Optional. Defaults to default . Defined in common\tributary_types\ percentage float Optional. Percentage of income the tributary gives to the suzerain. Defaults to the tributary type's definition.
Changes a character's military technology points by the specified amount.

Sets the specified variable to the remainder after division by the specified value or another variable. Can specify another scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be accessed from any scope. Also see variables .
Changes the morale of the unit by the specified amount.
Moves the scoped character to the target character's court. Also see force_host .

Multiplies the specified variable with a specified value or another variable. Can specify another scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be accessed from any scope. Also see variables .
Fires an event to scoped character. Uses a more elaborate window. See character_event .
Deprecated, use plot_succeeds and ambition_succeeds instead.
Scoped character gains occupation of all non-capital holdings in provinces inside the target character's realm where the capital holding has been sieged down by the scoped character or allies.

Adds an opinion modifier to the scoped character towards the target character. See also reverse_opinion . Parameter Type Description name opinion modifier Required. Opinion modifier to apply. who character Required. Towards who this opinion modifier is directed. months/years int Optional. Overrides the pre-defined opinion modifier duration. multiplier int Optional. How many stacks of the opinion modifier to apply. origin_description Key Optional. Localisation key used to display in the character pacts screen for alliance or non-aggression pact for opinion modifiers that establish one.
Changes decadence by the scoped character's war score percentage of the specified value.
Changes piety by the scoped character's war score percentage of the specified value.
Changes prestige by the scoped character's war score percentage of the specified value.
Changes a character's piety by the specified amount.
Pledges or unpledges a character to the defending side of a new-style Crusade in preparation phase.
Pledges or unpledges a character to the attacking side of a new-style Crusade in preparation phase.

Completes a character's plot and fires the plot's effect -block. Useful if a plot's success is difficult/expensive to detect by triggers, and/or a decision/event chain or anything else that can fire effects should complete the plot.
Changes a nomadic ruler's population by the specified amount.
Changes a characters's unpressed claim on a title into a pressed claim. Either the current scope or the target must be a character and the other must be a title.
Changes a character's prestige by the specified amount.

Lets the specified player rename the scoped entity. Parameter Type Description player character Required. Which player should get the prompt. type loc key What message type to display, as defined in messagetypes.txt. portrait character Optional. Which portrait to show on the right. If not defined, the scoped character (if scope is a character) will be used. name_list loc key Optional. Which name list to use. Can also use religion for religious names of the scoped character's religion, or culture for cultural names. If not specified, there will be no "randomize name" button (except for characters, that'll use the standard buttons for newborns). If using a loc key, customizable localization is supported. Loc keys contain various names supported by | : LOC_KEY;Name|Name2|Name3;;;;;;x .
Adds target character and descendants to scoped bloodline.
Fires an event to scoped province. See character_event .
Executes the enclosed effect with a specified base chance, optionally modified by various conditional modifiers. See random .
Executes one of the enclosed effect clauses with specified base chances, optionally modified by various modifiers. See random_list .
Province joins nearest ruler of the same religion and culture group, preferring same culture.
Recalculates the succession for all titles held by the scoped character.
Changes all remaining disease durations in the scoped province by their current remaining durations multiplied by the specified value. Note that disease duration is hidden.
Refills the scoped holding's garrison and levy.
Changes the (public) religion of scoped character/province/title. Can use a clause to specify which of the scope's religion to use, defaulting to public. See also unsafe_religion .

Adds a religion modifier to the religion of scoped character/province. Note: Once addded, religion modifiers cannot be removed. Parameter Type Description name religion modifier Required. Religion modifier to apply. days/months/years int Optional. Override the modifier's defined duration. Note: duration = -1 is NOT valid in this context! Instead, for permanent MA modifiers, use years = 5000 (or similar).
Remove the specified character from the scoped bloodline.
Removes the specified building from the scoped holding. Does not remove buildings that depend on this building, based on upgrades_from .

Removes a number of instances of a stacked character modifier . Currently bugged, always removing the entire stack. Work around it by keeping track of thet correct amount of stacked modifiers using variables.
Removes a claim on a title from a character. Either the current scope or the target must be a character and the other must be a title.
Removes the consort/concubine relationship between the scoped and target characters. Works in either scope.
Removes a modifier that applies to all members of the scoped character's dynasty.
Removes all evil god names from the scoped religion.
Target character no longer owes a favor to the scoped character. Also see reverse_remove_favor .
Ends a friendship between two characters.
Remove the scoped character from the specified bloodline. Note that the right-hand side must be a bloodline, not a bloodline type.
Removes all god names from the scoped religion.
Removes a number of instances of a stacked holding modifier .

Removes the scoped title from being a holy site of the given religion. Warning: this lets you have less than 5 holy sites which might cause weirdness. Also, removing holy sites to a religion but not its heresies will cause their icons to show up individually on other shared holy sites instead of being hidden like normal.

Removes the scoped title from being a holy site of the given religion and its heresies. Warning: this lets you have less than 5 holy sites which might cause weirdness. Note that if a religion does not have any heresies defined (e.g. Norse), remove_holy_site_with_heresies does nothing. Use remove_holy_site instead.
Forbids scoped religion to intermarry with target religion. One-way only, so apply converse intermarry separately, if desired. Also see add_intermarry and clear_intermarry .
Ends a romance between two characters.
Removes an opinion modifier from the scoped character towards the target character. Note: The opinion modifier will actually be removed on the next day tick (or on loading a save).
Removes a number of instances of a province modifier (usually a stackable one).
Ends a rivalry between two characters.
Removes a character's special title. See set_special_character_title .
Removes a character from the list of special interests, on the outliner, found on the right side of the screen.
Ends a marriage between two characters. yes removes all spouses.
Remove's a character's council position or minor title. Fires its lose_effect .
Removes a trait, also see add_trait .
Ends a tributary relationship between two characters. Can be used in either scope.
Decreases the number of available upgrade slots.

Fires an event, without changing the scope stack, by adding ROOT as FROM (i.e FROM , FROMFROM and so on remain unchanged). Note that it will fire the specified event, and not necessarily the current event again. See character_event . Warning : Firing a province event in a character scope or vice versa, will cause weird scopes ( ROOT and default will be different, and FROM will be modified), so this is not recommended.
Resets the coat of arms of the scoped title to its default.
Restores a previously saved succession law, see save_succession . Counts as a succession law change by the title holder.
Reveal the scoped character's plot to everyone, or only the target character.
See reveal_plot , but also sends all discoverers a letter event according to the configured message settings.
Makes the scoped character owe a favor to another character. Also see add_favor .
Similar to back_plot , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to banish , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to culture , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to imprison , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to leave_plot , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to opinion , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to religion , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to remove_favor , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to remove_opinion , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to set_opinion_levy_raised_days , but with the scopes reversed.
Similar to unsafe_war , but with the scopes reversed. See war for details.
Similar to war , but with the scopes reversed.
Makes an empty holding slot the county capital. Use on a capital holding. Also see make_capital_holding .
Removes the specified law from the scoped title. Commonly used in law effect clauses to remove all other laws in the same law group. Not used to remove succession and gender successsion laws.
Saves a reference to the current scope, to be re-used later in an unbroken event chain. See event targets .
Saves a global reference to the current scope, to be re-used later. See event targets .
Saves a reference to the specified scope in the current scope to be re-used later. name is the name of the reference, scope is the scope to save.
Saves a title's succession law, to be restored later using restore_succession .
Modifies piety by percent (1.0 = 100%) of annual piety increase. min increases final cost to min if result would be lower. max reduces the final cost to max if result would be lower.
Modifies prestige by percent (1.0 = 100%) of annual prestige increase. min increases final cost to min if result would be lower. max reduces the final cost to max if result would be lower.
Modifies wealth by percent (1.0 = 100%) of annual income. min increases final cost to min if result would be lower. max reduces the final cost to max if result would be lower.
Transfers ownership of the fort in the scoped county/province to the target character.
Transfers ownership of the trade post in the scoped county/province to the target character.
Emulates the effect of the Assassin-diplomatic interaction, firing one of the related on_actions , depending on relative intrigue.
Sets AI aggression for scoped religion (default: 1).
Toggles tyranny-free revocation of all vassal-held duchy titles.
Toggles tyranny-free revocation of all infidel vassals.
Toggles tyranny-free revocation of all vassals.
Toggles opinion malus of female rulers.
Toggles tyranny-free revocation of viceroyalty titles.
Toggles availability of female-centered gender laws.
Toggles matrilineal marriages for a religion. Not to be confused with law_set_allows_matrilineal_marriage , which determines that on a title level.
Toggles movement of fleets onto major rivers for a religion.
Allows granting viceroyalties of the specified tier and up, or disables granting of all viceroyalties.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped artifact.
Sets whether or not kingdoms and empires of this religion can have autocephalous religious heads. Implied by set_pentarchy = yes .
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped bloodline.
Sets which special traits to use if religion has no religious head. Branch tag can be defined with religious_branch in traits .
Sets whether or not brother-sister marriage is allowed for characters of the scoped religion.
Sets a special title flag, to be checked with has_councilor_faction_join_restriction .
Sets whether or not cousin marriage is allowed for characters of the scoped religion.
Sets whether or not a theocratic or temporal head of religion can call crusades.
Sets whether or not a theocratic head of religion can excommunicate characters of the same religion.
Sets whether or not a theocratic head of religion can grant title claims to characters of the same religion.
Sets whether or not a theocratic head of religion can grant divorces to characters of the same religion.
Sets whether or not a theocratic head of religion can grant an invasion CB on characters of the same religion. Disabling is bugged.
Sets whether or not a religion can have anti-religious heads set up. Incompatible with set_pentarchy = yes .
Enables or disables diplomatic interaction to have characters take the vows for characters of scoped religion.
Toggles the looting button on the scoped army scope.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped character.
Sets character modifiers for all characters of this religion, or removes it, if specified empty.
Sets the coats of arms (flag) of the scoped title to that of the target title. An otherwise unused "dummy" title in landed_titles can be used to define the coats of arms.
Sets AI behavior for converting outside their own religion group. 0 - never try to convert 1 - try to convert if ai_zeal is high 2 - always try to convert
Sets AI behavior for converting within their own religion group. 0 - never try to convert 1 - try to convert if ai_zeal is high 2 - always try to convert
Makes currently scoped character's council discontent for MONTHS_OF_DISCONTENT_COUNCIL months (vanilla value is 24).
Changes an artifact's creation date. Use -1 to set an unknown creation date.
Sets recipient of new-style Crusade target title.
Sets target to be the benificiary of new-style Crusade participant for the current character scope. Use none to unset beneficiary.
Multiplies war contribution for the purpose of crusade war chest distribution by specified factor. Does not modify actual war contribution. Set on a per-character basis.
Sets target of new-style Crusade. Character and title must be valid targets for the CB.
Sets the target scope as the new liege of the current scope. Either scope can be either a character or a title. Can be used to make a character become independent via set_defacto_liege = THIS .
Sets the current scope as the new liege for the target scope. Either scope can be either a character or a title. Can be used to make a character become independent via set_defacto_liege = THIS .
Sets whether or not provinces of this religion apply defensive attrition to armies of other religions when hostile.

Changes the description of the scoped to artifact or bloodline to the given string/localisation key. All custom localisation is resolved when set, so the description will not change once set. Can be reset by setting it to the blank string "" .
Sets the character to be "revealed" as part of the specified society, or otherwise their secret society if no society is specified.
Toggles the divine blood/marriage mechanism for scoped religion.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag to the scoped character's dynasty.
Changes the dynasty name of the scoped character.
Changes (or remove) the father of a character.
Sets whether or not priests of this religion can be female.
Sets whether or not female rulers and rulers with a female heir of this religion suffer negative vassal opinion.

Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the current scope, if it supports storing flags. Works for any such scope, unlike the more specific set_<scope>_flag commands. See storaging information . Note: Does not work on bloodline scope!
Sets a combat tactic for a flank in combat. Ignores both trigger and phase, but does carry out a phase change as part of the chosen tactic. [4]
Sets the focus of a character, ignoring the cooldown period. Also fires the focus' creation_effect -clause, as well as triggering on_focus_selected .
Sets the scoped character's gender to be male or female or the opposite of what they currently are. Warning: messing with a character's gender may have unintended side effects so use with caution.
Sets (or resets the date on) a global flag .
Change the government type of a character. As of 2.8, forces immediate government validation, ensuring the character can enact the target government type.
Sets the ethnicity (but not clothing) of a character, based on the default graphical_culture of the target's culture.
Target character becomes guardian of scoped character.
Sets whether or not (provinces of) the scoped religion are hard to convert.
Sets whether or not characters of this religion can designate their heir. Requires Rajas of India DLC to function.

Sets the scoped title to be a holy site of the given religion. Warning: this lets you have more than 5 holy sites which might cause weirdness. Also, adding holy sites to a religion but not its heresies will cause their icons to show up individually on other shared holy sites instead of being hidden like normal. If target is a title, uses religion of titleholder. If target is a province, uses province religion.
Sets the scoped title to be a holy site of the given religion and its heresies. Warning: this lets you have more than 5 holy sites which might cause weirdness.
Sets the religion's high god's name to the given key.
Sets whether or not armies of this religion are affected by defensive attrition of unreformed pagans.
Sets a character as important.  They will neither be removed from AI courts nor be deleted from the saved game to reduce file size. WARNING: This cannot be reversed.
Make a character interested in joining the specified society.
Toggles investiture between the religion head and the title holder.
Enables or disables infidel tax on holdings in provinces of a different religion group
Sets (or resets) the council job of a councillor, in a specific location.
Sets characters hostile, without requiring a war or looting.
Toggles looting status of the scoped army.
Sets whether or not priests of this religion can be male.
Sets how many consorts man and women of this religion can have. Also works for society ranks; see the 3.0/Holy Fury patch notes .
Sets how many wives men of this religion can have. Does not apply to women.
Sets the religion's men_can_take_consorts attribute to the given value. Also works for society ranks; see the 3.0/Holy Fury patch notes .
Change (or remove) the mother of a character.

Override name of character or title. Using set_name = "" resets the name to the original. You can also use a scope of the same type as the thing being renamed. Note that for artifacts this will use the name after processing localisation, so all custom localisation will become static upon doing so.
Sets a religion to not have a religious head on reformation.
Sets the official new-style Crusade recipient. Also see official_crusade_recipient scope.
Sets the scoped character's total amount of offmap currency for the specified offmap power to the value .
Sets the dislike of the specified offmap power to the specified type .  May use random to switch to a random dislike.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped offmap power.
Sets the scoped offmap power's current ruler to the target scope.
Sets the like of the specified offmap power to the specified type .  May use random to switch to a random like.
Sets the scoped offmap power's name to the localisation key corresponding to the string.
Sets (or resets the date on) a temporary flag in the scoped offmap power.
Sets  the duration over which the scoped character gains an opinion malus towards their liege for having raised their levies.
Changes the original owner of an artifact.

Prevents character from declaring war on others in the same realm for specified duration. There is no associated trigger, this is checked in the hardcoded declaration triggers, before selecting a casus belli. Can be annulled with parameter 0.
Religion becomes an heresy of new parent religion.
Sets whether or not parent-child marriage is allowed for characters of the scoped religion.
Sets monthly piety gain for characters of this religion while at peace.
Enables/disables monthly prestige loss for characters of this religion while at peace for too long.
Sets (or removes) the Pentarch seat that governs the scoped title.
Sets whether or not realms of this religion can follow pentarch seats. Also see set_pentarch_title . Incompatible with set_can_have_antipopes = yes .
Sets a different picture to be shown for the scoped artifact.
Toggles monthly piety loss when characters of this religion are at war with same religion characters.

The player controlling the scoped character starts controlling the given character instead. Does not enforce remaining within the same dynasty. WARNING : It's possible to cause game overs with this, so use with care.
Sets the scoped offmap power's current policy to the specified ID (corresponding to a policy in /common/offmap_powers/policies).

Sets the de jure capital of the scoped title to the specified province/title. If the right-hand side is a barony or county title, sets capital to the corresponding province, for higher tier titles, uses the de jure capital province of that title. Works for both dynamic and static titles since patch 2.8. Also takes relative scopes (FROM, ROOT, PREV etc.) and saved event targets.
Sets whether or not priests of this religion can inherit landed titles.
Sets whether or not priests of this religion can marry.
Toggles blocking titles leaving the realm due to outside inheritance.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped province.
Sets whether or not uncle-niece and aunt-nephew marriages are allowed for characters of the scoped religion.
Creates a quest for the scoped character.

Creates a quest targeting the current scope or changes the target of an already exist target to the scope. Parameter Type Description id quest_id The name of the quest. Dynamic and can be anything (though requires localisation). holder character The character who receives the quest, or who has it already. society society Optional, defaults to the character's society. If the society is not set, and the character is not part of a society, this will send an error and nothing will happen.
Sets whether or not characters suffer vassal opinion when raising vassal troops.
Changes (or removes) the real father of a character, for example a bastard child.
Sets the scoped character as being reincarnated from the target character. Use 0 to remove the link. Also see reincarnation_scope .
Sets the religion's rel_head_defense attribute to the given value.

Sets the title that controls the religion. Use none to set the religion as not having any controller. If a title already controls the religion when this is called, it will cease to control the religion.

Sets religion to use a set of branch traits (see Dharmic sects and pagan branch traits). Can take a religion ID (hindu), or a custom key which must be matched in trait definitions , using religious_branch = hindu/pagan_reformation .
Sets whether or not AI will prefer raiding coastal provinces.
Sets the secret religion of the character to the right-hand-side (defaulting to secret religion, if applicable). Can be expanded to specify what visibility to use.
Sets the title's short_name parameter to the given value.See title flags .
Sets short reign opinion malus multiplier.
Sets how much income the dynamic mercenary title pays to its creator.
Set or unset the scoped character as the grandmaster of their society.
Set the society's current progress to a given value.
Gives a character a special title, overriding their title determined by both landed and minor titles. Persists after death.
Sets the scoped offmap power's current status modifier to the specified ID (corresponding to a modifier in /common/offmap_powers/statuses).
Toggles if vassals are able to wage war against both internal and external targets.
Toggles if vassals are able to wage war against other vassals.
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped title.
Toggles a title's adventurer attribute. See create_title .
Toggles a title's landless attribute. See create_title .
Toggles a title's nomad attribute. See create_title .
Changes the base value of a trade route, before any modifiers from trade route buildings are applied.
Changes the base multiplier of a trade route, before any other modifiers are applied. Setting it to 0 effectively disables the trade route.

Whether liege can directly raise tribal vassal levies. Note: Despite the very literal name of this command, its effect may not be limited to tribal vassals; instead, it may work for all vassals which are called to arms instead of granting levies. (Not verified, is based on a discord support question, needs testing.)
Whether tribal vassals pay taxes to their liege. Note: May be usable in a wider context (see set_tribal_vassal_levy_control ).

Creates a truce on the scoped character, towards the target character, for the specified duration. Overrides any previously-existing truce between the two characters. Can be used to remove a truce by setting a zero duration ( days = 0 ).
Sets modifiers for all units owned by characters of scoped religion.
Sets modifiers for all units in owned by characters of scoped religion, when in province of matching religion.

    land_morale = 0.8
    light_infantry_defensive = 0.8
    heavy_infantry_defensive = 0.8

    knights_defensive = 0.8
    archers_defensive = 0.8
    horse_archers_defensive = 0.8
    camel_cavalry_defensive = 0.8

}
Sets whether or not religion uses decadence mechanic.

Used to create (or reset) a variable to a value, or to the value of another variable. Can specify another another scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be set from any scope. Also see variables .
Sets the religion's women_can_take_consorts attribute to the given value. Also works for society ranks; see the 3.0/Holy Fury patch notes .
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped wonder.
Sets a wonder to use the specified model, defined in interface\wonder_mesh.gfx
Sets (or resets the date on) a flag in the scoped wonder upgrade.
Fires a quest event to scoped character. See character_event .
Rank down a character by the specified number of ranks in their current society, or the society specified if applicable.
Rank up a character by the specified number of ranks in their current society, or the society specified if applicable.
Plays the specified sound, as defined in interface/sound.sfx.
Spawns a specific disease in the scoped province.

Parameter Type Description province province/closest Closest sea zone owner character earmark earmark ID of the unit, to be able to reference them later. troops clause Fixed amount of troops in the form troop_type = { <max_value> <starting_value> } . Ex: galleys = { 20 20 } match_character character match_mult float Matches against the total levies of every single holding match_min float disband_on_peace bool cannot_inherit bool

Only owner and province are required. Parameter Type Description province province/title/closest/ closest_to_capital Spawn location. Uses de jure capital for titles above count tier. home province Source for troop technology bonuses. owner character Ruler who gains this army, defaults to scoped character. leader character/none Leader to appoint to this army. Defaults to the owner, followed by the owner's available commanders. earmark string ID of the unit, for later use with disband_event_forces and has_earmarked_regiments(_not_raiding) . Can be localized via earmark _ARMY and earmark _ARMY_OF. troops clause Base troop sizes in the form <troop_type> = { <max_value> <starting_value> } . match_character character Character to match against for match_mult match_settlement barony title Holding to match against for match_mult . match_mult float Multiplies the base troop numbers by this number * match_character 's total levy size (levies and event troops) or match_settlement 's (current garrison and levies combined) match_max float Upper boundary for match_character/settlement match_min float Lower boundary for match_character/settlement scaled_by_biggest_garrison float Multiplies the base troop sizes by the given factor * sum of the province's maximum levy and garrison size / 20 scaled_by_tax bool Multiplies the base troop sizes by the sum of all base tax bonuses on normal holdings and buildings in the province. Also sets maintenance to 0. scaled_with_population_of character Scales army size to target nomad's population, in tandem with for_population for_population float Base troop sizes are multiplied by scaled_with_population_of divided by for_population attrition float Multiplier to base army attrition rate maintenance_multiplier float Multiplier to base troop maintenance cost. reinforces bool Allows spawned army to reinforce. reinforce_rate_multiplier float Multiplier to base reinforcement rate. disband_on_peace bool Forces the spawned army to disband once its owner is at peace. cannot_inherit bool Cannot be inherited on owner's death. merge bool Merge all the armies in this province together into one army. can_toggle_looting bool Allows spawned army to toggle looting. is_looter bool Allows spawned army to loot.

Starts a faction on the liege of the current character scope, if it does not already exist. Different arguments are required depending on the type of the faction being started: character: faction liege_titles: faction, title liege_titles_w_claimant: faction, title, thirdparty The optional can_join_existing argument controls whether or not the character will join the faction if it already exists, with the default behaviour being no.
Forces an outbreak, but follows the scenarios set up in the disease.txt file.
Ends a feud between two clans
Steals a percentage of the population from another nomad clan.

Increases, by a whole level, a random technology in the target province out of all technologies that are at least one increment level higher in the scoped province. Uses de jure capital of target title, uses capital province of target character (or of their liege, if unlanded). Does nothing if no technologies in the source province are at least one increment higher than in the target province. May increase a technology beyond the level in the source province. Also see has_higher_tech_than .
Similar to vassalize_or_take_under_title , but also applies opinion_subjugated(_other_rel) to all vassalised rulers.
Subtract specified value or another variable to a variable. Can specify a scope from which to take the second variable. Global and local variables can be accessed from any scope. Also see variables .

Changes the title's succession law, but does not count as changing the succession law, letting the ruler change it later on. Either a hard-coded succession type: gavelkind , primogeniture , seniority , ultimogeniture , turkish_succession , papal_succession , appointment , open_elective , catholic_bishopric , patrician_elective , nomad_succession , offmap_succession . Or a clause consisting of an elective base_type ( feudal_elective , elective_gavelkind , or tanistry ) and voting_rules token (defined in common/succession_voting) The latter can also be set separately using the elective_voting_rules command.
Similar to succession , but counts as changing the succession law. Does not add the cooldown for non-succession laws.
Transfers the artifact from one character to another. If from does not have the artifact, it will not be transferred.

Transfers wealth from one character to another, equal to value multiplied by the sender's gross yearly income (demesne, tax, tribute, trade). If from is specified as the sender, the current scope is the recipient, and vice versa. Parameter Type Description from character Either from or to to character Either from or to value all/float 1 means 1 year of income min float min = 5 max float max = 50 Warning: The min parameter does not always work! For unlanded characters and those with very low monthly_income (approx < 1), zero gold is transferred. For characters whose wealth cannot be negative (?!?!!), some gold will be transferred, but only until they reach a zero balance. Recommendation: Do NOT use this command for unlanded characters, or for those with low monthly_income . Instead, detect those characters using if/else logic, and directly transfer the money using the wealth command.
Executes an effect based on various values of a single condition, with an optional fallback. Need not use all possible values of the used trigger. See switch .
Changes the current size of the unit by the amount indicated. Values are percentages of the unit's maximum size, with 1.0 equal to 100%. Does not allow units to grow beyond their maximum size.
Fires an event to scoped character. Rarely used. See character_event .
Similar to destroy_artifact , but can also destroy indestructible artifacts.
Bypasses some error-checking in destroy title, allowing to destroy landless titles. Warning: Use this effect with care!

See impregnate , but ignores existing pregnancies, adding a new one.
See impregnate_cuckoo , but ignores existing pregnancies, adding a new one.
See religion , but allows to change the religion of the leader of a holy order, a religious head or a rebel leader.
Works like the war command, but without ensuring the CB can be used. See war for details.

Similar to gain_title , but also applies opinion_usurped_title and a strong pressed claim to the current holder. The recipient retains their liege, if possible. Fires on_new_holder_usurpation , regardless of the type used, see gain_title .
Similar to usurp_title , but also mentions the usurpation in the title history. Equal to usurp_title with type = usurp .
Combines gain_title_plus_barony_if_unlanded and usurp_title . If the recipient is not a ruler, requires the title to be currently held.
Similar to gain_settlements_under_title , but vassalises as many rulers as possible, only taking holdings of rulers who also hold lands outside the target title.
Similar to vassalize_or_take_under_title , but destroys all duchies titles held by vassalised rulers.

Initiate a war, with current character as attacker. Also see unsafe_war , reverse_war and reverse_unsafe_war . Parameter Type Description target character/title The character to declare war on. casus_belli key The casus belli to use for this war. thirdparty_title title/province Optional. The title/province to declare war for. thirdparty character Optional. The character to declare war on behalf of. tier tier Optional. Which de jure liege title of thirdparty_title this war targets instead. plot_backers bool Optional. Makes attacker's plot backers join the war. faction key Optional. Which faction should join the war. infamy int Optional. Percentage of regular infamy this war accrues. For technical reasons, thirdparty claimant wars require the current scope to be the claimant and thirdparty the attacker. All other CBs work intuitively, using above syntax.
